title: A two-phase prospective observational study to identify and validate hyperspectral features of peritoneal tumour manifestations in gastrointestinal and pancreatic-biliary adenocarcinomas
summary:
Tumour deposits in the peritoneum, known as peritoneal carcinomatosis, are a common consequence of malignant diseases of the abdominal organs and the biliary tract. Depending on the type of the original tumour, such peritoneal deposits occur with varying frequency. Their presence has an important influence on further treatment and the course of the disease. Even modern imaging techniques such as computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging or ultrasound have only limited accuracy in detecting small peritoneal deposits. Therefore, involvement of the peritoneum can often only be reliably detected or excluded during an exploratory laparoscopic operation. The assessment of whether peritoneal deposits are present and how extensive they are is currently based on direct inspection of the abdominal cavity by the surgeon. However, this assessment may be influenced by the visibility of the operative field and the surgeon’s experience. For standardisation, the so-called Peritoneal Carcinomatosis Index (PCI) is used. However, this well-researched and established system is also based on visual assessment during the operation. Hyperspectral imaging is a modern camera-based technique that, in addition to normal images, can provide further information about tissue characteristics, for example blood perfusion, oxygen saturation or water content. This information is obtained through light measurements. No radiation, contrast agents or additional medicines are used.

The aim of the study is to investigate whether this additional information can help to improve the detection of tumour tissue in the abdominal cavity and further objectify the assessment of the PCI.
conditions: Tumourmanifestations in the peritoneum, Peritoneal carcinomatosis

interventions.name:
Study protocol (both phases identical, analysis carried out separately):
Intraoperative procedure: Standard laparoscopy under white light (clinical standard)
- Systematic inspection according to PCI regions
- Storage of standardised white-light images for each region (for secondary PCI analyses)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Confirmed diagnosis or imaging findings highly suspicious for gastrointestinal or pancreatico-biliary adenocarcinoma
• Indication for diagnostic laparoscopy (clinical standard)
• Feasibility of using the TIVITA Mini®
• Written informed consent
• If applicable, negative pregnancy test (within 72 h)
Exclusion criteria:
• Contraindications according to the manufacturer’s instructions
• Lack of capacity to provide informed consent
• Placement in an institution by administrative or court order
• Pregnancy/lactation
